title: zshrc, zprofile and zshenv: which file to edit on macOS
summary: zsh reads a few hidden setup files when a Terminal session starts. Most personal changes go in ~/.zshrc, and ~/.zprofile is for one-time login setup; ~/.zshenv is rarely needed.

aliases.text: which zsh file to edit mac
в каком файле настройки терминала на маке

steps.explain: zsh reads its startup files in this order: ~/.zshenv for every zsh, then ~/.zprofile for login shells, then ~/.zshrc for interactive shells, and finally ~/.zlogin for login shells. Files in /etc are read as well, but beginners do not need them.
Put most personal changes into ~/.zshrc, such as aliases, prompt settings, and extra folders added to PATH. zsh reads it for every new interactive window or tab in Terminal.
Use ~/.zprofile for setup that should run once when you log in, not in every tab. Installers such as Homebrew often ask you to put their PATH setup here.
Leave ~/.zshenv alone unless you have a clear reason. zsh reads it for every zsh, including ones started by scripts, so keep it very small and never print text from it.
Open a new Terminal window after you change one of these files. Windows that were already open keep the old settings.
